description: Ohio-only rules checked against the Revised Code sections cited on each question. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Ohio's school-zone limit is 20 mph when
options: A school is within a mile, at any hour
Signs are up, at recess or opening/closing hours
The limit is 20 only while a bus is stopped
questions.explanation: R.C. 4511.21(B)(1)(a), effective June 30, 2025. On a controlled-access highway or freeway whose right-of-way fence has no pedestrian opening, that school-zone rule does not apply. 20 mph school signs are erected, and it is school recess or the opening or closing hours while children are going to or leaving school.

questions.q: In an Ohio municipal corporation, the prima facie limit on streets that are not the listed exceptions is
questions.explanation: R.C. 4511.21(B)(2) sets 25 mph in other portions of a municipal corporation. The exceptions include state routes outside business districts, through highways outside business districts, and alleys.

questions.q: The speed limit on an alley in an Ohio municipal corporation is
questions.explanation: R.C. 4511.21(B)(7) sets 15 mph on alleys within the municipal corporation.

questions.q: R.C. 4511.21 sets 70 mph on
options: Every freeway, including urban freeways with signals
questions.explanation: Division (B)(14) sets 70 mph on all rural freeways. Division (B)(16) sets 65 mph on freeways or expressways without traffic signals in urbanized areas. Division (B)(15) sets 55 mph on designated congested freeway portions inside a municipal corporation or an interstate outerbelt.

questions.q: The general Ohio limit on highways outside a municipal corporation, before the freeway and other listed exceptions, is
questions.explanation: R.C. 4511.21(B)(5) sets 55 mph on highways outside municipal corporations, then carves out island roads, named highway classes, and the freeway limits.

questions.q: The Ohio registrar imposes a class D license suspension when points within a two-year period reach
questions.explanation: R.C. 4510.037(B) uses any two-year period that begins on the date of the first conviction in that period. The notice says the suspension is effective on the 20th day after mailing unless the person appeals. 12 or more.

questions.q: For the first 12 months, an Ohio probationary-license holder may not drive between midnight and 6 a.m. unless
options: The trip is under five miles
A parent or guardian rides along
Any licensed adult is in the car
questions.explanation: R.C. 4507.071. The midnight-to-6 a.m. ban does not apply to travel to or from work, a school function, or a religious event when the holder carries the documentation that subsection requires. A parent or guardian is with the holder, or a listed exception applies.

questions.q: In Ohio, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Ohio issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Section 4507.05 | Temporary instruction permit - temporary instruction permit identification card.

questions.q: In Ohio, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Ohio requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Ohio complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Ohio requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Section 4507.21 | Application for and issuance of license.

questions.q: Of a Ohio teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Ohio requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: Section 4507.21 | Application for and issuance of license.

questions.q: In Ohio, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Ohio, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Ohio not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Ohio restricts provisional drivers from Midnight to 6 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

questions.q: In Ohio, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Ohio drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: Section 4507.01 | Driver's license law definitions - authority of registrar - deputy registrars.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Ohio car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Ohio car knowledge test has 40 questions.

provenance.manual: Driver License & ID Cards - Ohio BMV

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Ohio car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 75% to pass the Ohio car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Driver License & ID Cards - Ohio BMV

questions.q: In Ohio, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Ohio, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: Section 4511.19 | Operating vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs - OVI.

questions.q: In Ohio, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Ohio sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Section 4511.19 | Operating vehicle under the influence of alcohol or drugs - OVI.

questions.q: In Ohio, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Ohio brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: Unless a sign says otherwise, what is the speed limit in a Ohio residential district?
questions.explanation: Ohio sets 25 mph in residential districts unless another limit is posted.

provenance.manual: Section 4511.21 | Speed limits - assured clear distance.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Ohio?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Ohio can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Ohio's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Ohio: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Ohio?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Ohio, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Ohio's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Ohio seat belt enforcement is secondary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Ohio?
questions.explanation: Ohio requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: Section 4511.81 | Child restraint system - child highway safety fund.

questions.q: What is Ohio's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Ohio requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

questions.q: Under Ohio's point system, what is the lowest point total that can suspend an adult's license?
questions.explanation: Ohio can suspend an adult's license at 12 points in 24 months.
